findings.quote: at most two stades from the city
findings.problem: τόπος ἀπέχων μὲν τῆς πόλεως δύο μάλιστα σταδίους: μάλιστα with a number means 'about', not 'at most'.
findings.proposed_fix: about two stades from the city

findings.quote: As the day was already drawing on
findings.problem: ἤδη δὲ τῆς ὥρας συναγούσης: ὥρα here is the season of the year (the campaigning season closing, autumn), not the hour of the day.
findings.proposed_fix: As the season was already drawing to a close

units.note: Greek breaks off mid-sentence at the end (οὗτος μὲν αὖτις ἐξ / Ἐλατείας ἀνέστρεφε in ch. 27); the failure of the king's plan (διαπεσούσης τῆς ἐπιβολῆς) is carried by the opening of ch. 27, not lost.
Opening 'When the expedition failed' completes the sentence begun at end of ch. 26 (διαπεσούσης δ᾽ αὐτῷ τῆς ἐπιβολῆς); acceptable.

findings.quote: promising that they would bring the Aetolians to agree to whatever was necessary for making peace
findings.problem: ὑπισχνούμενοι πάντα ποιήσειν τοὺς Αἰτωλοὺς ἐφ᾽ ᾧ συνθέσθαι τὴν εἰρήνην: the Aetolians are the subject of ποιήσειν (the Aetolians would do everything to conclude peace), not the envoys bringing the Aetolians round.
findings.proposed_fix: promising that the Aetolians would do everything required to conclude the peace

findings.quote: The Aetolians, who had been hoping to exploit the situation in their own favor, were now eager to conclude peace
findings.problem: Greek has only οἱ δ᾽ Αἰτωλοὶ τὰ μὲν ἔσπευδον ποιήσασθαι τὴν εἰρήνην (they were, on the one hand, eager for peace, pressed by the war); there is no clause about hoping to exploit the situation. The μὲν is answered by ἅμα δὲ ... παρεῖλκον below.
findings.proposed_fix: The Aetolians, for their part, were eager to conclude peace

units.note: Numbers (1300 Aetolians, 1000 foot, 200 horse, about 3000) agree with the Greek.

English paragraph 3 ('My reason is that I believe this arrangement will best keep readers...') has no separate Greek counterpart and partly doubles paragraph 4 (which renders τοῦ μὲν γὰρ μὴ ... διαμαρτάνειν); Greek says 'sufficient' (ἱκανήν), not 'best'. Not a sense inversion, so no finding; flag to editor if desired.
